Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Carlos Diaz (Meridian CTO), Maya Patel (Meridian SRE Lead), Ethan Liu (Meridian Product)
summary: Discovery focused on reliability and incident tolerance across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment options. Discussed multi-region routing, automatic fallback policies (model variants and region fallback), p99/p95 latency targets, burst capacity and reserved capacity tradeoffs, SLAs and compliance items (audit logs, KMS, SOC2). Agreed next steps to share routing doc, run benchmarks, and schedule POC kickoff.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call — I'm Alex, AE on the account, with Priya our solutions engineer.
[00:00:10] Carlos (Meridian CTO): Hi Alex, hi Priya, Carlos here. Maya and Ethan on from our side.
[00:00:15] Maya (Meridian SRE): Hi.
[00:00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. High level today — want to understand your reliability constraints and how you'd expect Redwood to behave in incidents, esp multi-region failures and how fallbacks should be orchestrated.
[00:00:30] Ethan (Product): Yeah we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for our checkout and fraud models. Main ask is: if a region fails, what happens to latency, cost, and data residency?
[00:00:42] Alex: Awesome. Maybe start with your current setup — Maya?
[00:00:45] Maya: Sure. We run core services in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, CICD across both. For ML we have a mix: some on-prem GPUs and some inference endpoints in BigCloudAI. Our SLOs for checkout are p99 < 250ms for the validation step, and overall end-to-end 500ms. We do burst traffic during promotions — 3x baseline for short windows.
[00:01:10] Priya: Thanks, that's helpful. Two big levers to hit latency and capacity: reserved/dedicated pools vs hosted with autoscaling and burst. For Dedicated you get reserved capacity so p99 is more predictable but you pay for the commit. Hosted gives flexibility and rapid failover to other regions but can have cold-start jitter if capacity needs to be provisioned.
[00:01:35] Carlos: In an incident we want deterministic behavior — e.g., if us-east has networking issues we need automatic cross-region failover within 10s and clear fallbacks, and a fallback to a cheaper model if the top-tier model is unavailable. Is that something Redwood supports natively?
[00:01:48] Priya: Yes. We support multi-region routing policies that can be configured by priority or latency thresholds. Primary route is regional hosted endpoint; if unhealthy, traffic can be routed to a secondary region or to a fallback model variant (lower memory / quantized). The routing is done at the control plane with health checks; failover typically happens within tens of seconds depending on cache warming.
[00:02:12] Maya: Cache warming is our concern — if KV cache is cold across regions, p99 will spike. What do you do about prefix cache and key-value cache across regions?
[00:02:22] Priya: Good question. We do prefix/KV cache warming strategies: warm on fallback by shipping a small set of hot prefixes, and we can keep a cross-region read-only cache using mirrored warm sets. Practically, in our Hosted product we maintain a hot set for each tenant; when failover happens we have a short warm-up window and we also support synchronous KV fetch from persistent store to avoid huge spikes. That said, during the first heavy-failover window p95/p99 can degrade, so we often recommend an intermediate fallback: route to a smaller model variant that has lower latency and smaller KV footprint.
[00:02:58] Ethan: So you can fallback to say a 7B quantized model if the 70B is unavailable?
[00:03:02] Priya: Exactly. We support model variant families and automatic model substitution. You can define a fallback graph: region -> model variant -> degraded feature flags.
[00:03:12] Alex: And for Dedicated customers you can pin capacity per region and set a hot standby region that's reserved; we also support burst capacity across a shared pool if you enable burst. That reduces failover latency because kernels are already loaded.
[00:03:25] Carlos: And in terms of SLAs, what do you guarantee for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[00:03:29] Alex: Our standard hosted SLA covers availability of the control plane and best-effort latency targets, but Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime (99.9% or higher depending on contract) and tail latency targets based on instance types. We'll share the SLA matrix in the doc pack.
[00:03:42] Maya: Is there a rolling degrade policy? Like in a multi-region outage do you fail traffic over incrementally or all at once?
[00:03:49] Priya: You can choose. We have canary failover (gradual routing shift), instantaneous failover, or policy-based where traffic is shifted based on observed latency thresholds and error rates. Canary is recommended for big services so you can catch regressions.
[00:04:05] Ethan: Can we set separate policies per endpoint? e.g., checkout needs stricter controls than our internal personalization.
[00:04:09] Priya: Yes, routing and fallbacks are per-route. You can also attach cost thresholds — if fallback to a secondary region increases cost above X, we can opt to degrade features instead of shipping to that region.
[00:04:21] Carlos: About observability — we need token-level cost attribution and tracing so we can reconcile cost with p99 impacts. How mature are your dashboards?
[00:04:30] Alex: Redwood Console gives per-route and per-model dashboards, p50/p95/p99, trace samples, and token-level cost breakdowns. You also get an audit log for control-plane changes and access events. For Private deployments audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM.
[00:04:42] Maya: KMS / HSM integration? We need customer-managed keys for some PII features.
[00:04:46] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CloudKMS) and support HSM-backed envelopes. Keys never leave your control plane on Private; in Hosted we support CMK with envelope encryption. We'll share the exact flow in the security doc.
[00:05:00] Ethan: Any limitations around data residency if we route across regions during failover?
[00:05:04] Alex: Good point. If you require strict residency, you can disable cross-region fallback for specific datasets. We also offer Private deployments where the control plane is customer-managed and data never leaves the VPC.
[00:05:15] Carlos: On the compliance front, we need SOC 2 + ISO mention and an audit-ready package.
[00:05:19] Priya: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 docs, plus an enterprise compliance pack that includes SOC reports, pen test summary, and our runbooks. We'll attach that.
[00:05:29] Maya: Back to incident tolerance: how do you handle degraded model outputs? For fraud models, false positives are dangerous. Do you do shadowing or staged rollbacks?
[00:05:39] Priya: Yes, we recommend a staged approach. You can shadow traffic to a model variant and run quality checks before switching live. We also support automatic rollback rules based on evaluation metrics (precision/recall deltas). For high-risk flows like fraud we often do canary + human-in-loop thresholds.
[00:05:55] Ethan: Pricing — any changes if we use cross-region fallback or burst across Dedicated pools?
[00:06:00] Alex: Dedicated is a predictably priced commit; burst usage is billed as overage on top of the commit. Cross-region egress is metered; we'll include examples in the cost model. Also fallback to cheaper quantized models reduces per-token cost.
[00:06:12] Carlos: One last thing — runbooks and on-call integration. We need PagerDuty hooks and a way to trigger capacity increases.
[00:06:19] Priya: You can connect Redwood alerts to PagerDuty, Slack, and Webhooks. We also have APIs to increase reserved capacity and trigger a scaling event, though in Dedicated scale is policy-driven.
[00:06:30] Alex: Cool — sounds like we have alignment on most items. Next steps: we'll send the routing/fallback doc, security pack, and a proposed POC plan. Priya will run a bench to show p95/p99 impact during failover.
[00:06:42] Maya: Sounds good. We'll share our infra diagram and SLOs.
[00:06:46] Carlos: Thanks, appreciate it.
[00:06:48] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the POC kickoff.
[00:06:55] Speaker 2: (inaudible)
[00:07:00] End of recording.

Notes: Transcription had occasional mislabels; references to KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash. Shared artifacts mentioned: multi-region-routing-playbook.pdf (Alex), security-compliance-pack.zip (Alex), bench-results-template.xlsx (Priya).
